newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Costello sees reducing interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Costello sees reducing interest rates.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello on Monday said the government projected an outlook of falling interest rates and good economic growth.
"Where do we see the government going? Into a surplus, reducing interest rates, growth amongst the best of any of the OECD nations," Costello told parliament.
The government has argued that its economic policies will produce interest rates lower than they would have been without its reforms.
The Reserve Bank has cut official cash rates a total of 200 basis points, to 5.5 percent, in four equal cuts from July 1996 to May 23 this year.
Economists now generally expect a better than even chance of another reduction due to weak economic data, including continuing high unemployment.
Unemployment was 8.8 percent in May, up from 8.7 percent a year earlier.
The government's budget for the fiscal year from July, released in May, projected economic growth of 3.75 percent in 1997/98 from 3.25 percent in 1996/97.

It also forecast the underlying deficit -- excluding asset sales and state government debt repayments -- to move into a A$1.6 billion surplus in 1998/99, from a A$6.9 billion deficit in 1996/97 and a A$3.9 billion deficit in 1997/98.
